verses.author: model_A
verses.text: The last snow melts from the roof tiles one drop at a time.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
the gutter still holds
what the winter left behind—
one bright coin of ice

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
a sparrow lands there
tilts its head to drink the light
before it finds water

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
it drinks anyway—
light and water taste the same
to a thirsty bird

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
the coin grows smaller
each time its beak touches down—
spring paid in small change

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
by dusk the gutter's empty—
some debt always gets settled

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
the sparrow's shadow
overdraws its own small account—
dark bill, nothing left

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
moonrise on the wire—
someone somewhere calls it interest
the bird just calls it home

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
morning collects the wire's
loose change of frost—
the sparrow spends it singing

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
the sparrow's ledger closes
with one clean note—
nothing owed, nothing left to keep

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
empty branch, empty pocket—
the wire still hums
the interest of leaving

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
somewhere the hum becomes
a phone line, a voice saying
call me when it's spring again

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
spring keeps no calendar
but the wire remembers
every voice it carried

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
the wire hums my mother's name
into static—
I keep the line open anyway

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
the static settles like snow
on a name I still dial
just to hear it ring

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
no one answers
but the ringing keeps a shape
I lay my ear against
